report.code_assessment: The code follows the spec very closely. Nearly every module names the scope it implements in its doc comment, and the scope's specific numbers, labels, colours, file paths and behaviours turn up in the code almost word for word. This holds across prompt mode, the chat input, the container environment, the ribbon, divergence, rescope, run targets, self-update and the theme. Real divergences are few and small: the Application tab adds a Reset Brightness command the spec doesn't have, the shared sidebar panel header is drawn on the darkest surface instead of the raised surface the SidebarScope gives, and the harness's built-in agents are hard-coded. A few module doc comments are out of date and describe older behaviour: random hidden-anchor names, a file splitting the view, four chat tabs, and every ribbon command being primary. Most of what the implementation decided on its own is internal plumbing that the spec reasonably leaves open, such as virtualized measuring, disk watching, hit testing, polling intervals, parsing harness and shell output, and test tooling.
report.spec_assessment: The spec is unusually complete and precise. Almost every scope gives exact strings, pixel sizes, colours, keyboard shortcuts, timings and edge cases, so an implementation has very little to guess. The code follows it closely: every scope I checked has a module that implements it. Those modules repeat the spec's own wording in doc comments, user-facing strings and constants (768 px scroll barrier, 400-file cap, 10 s timeouts, 6-hour update checks), and tests are named after its behaviours. The clearest divergence I found is in the edge-release workflow: it only builds the tests rather than running them, and it publishes releases with --latest instead of marking them as pre-releases, both against the spec. A smaller gap is that the theme spec has no darkest-surface or ribbon roles, so the code adds roles of its own for them. The agent skill and command files and the abstract lib anchors describe tooling that Belay compiles, not application code, so nothing in src traces to them. In the scopes being edited now (Ask cards and mode system prompts), the spec and code changes appear to be moving together.

well_defined.name: Prompt mode, chat input and sending
well_defined.why: The PromptEditor, MessageList, ChatInputScope, PromptSendingScope, QueueListScope and PromptModesScope specify lanes, chains, previews, history, naming, escaping, filters and scrolling in exhaustive detail, and the code mirrors them nearly one to one.

well_defined.name: Container environment and harness integration
well_defined.why: The ContainerEnvironmentScope and HarnessIntegrationScope give exact mounts, volumes, session folders, Podman failure handling, per-harness CLI flags, feeding and background-task rules, which container.rs and harness.rs implement directly.

well_defined.name: Mode system prompts and fluency files
well_defined.why: Placeholders, paragraph-dropping rules, file locations, the defaults and the card format are all spelled out, leaving system_prompts.rs, piton_fluency.rs and suspense_fluency.rs little to invent.

well_defined.name: Analysis panels (divergence, rescope, generate skills, run targets)
well_defined.why: Each scope fixes its steps, agent prompts, reply shapes, scoring formulas, layout, tooltips and saving, so the view and model files are written almost straight from them.

well_defined.name: Reusable UI components
well_defined.why: The ribbon, scrollbar, file tree, git panel, diff view, fs browser, inset and minimizable panels, project indicator, walkthrough and welcome scopes give pixel sizes, colours and keyboard behaviour that the code adopts as constants.

well_defined.name: Theme, brightness and preferences
well_defined.why: The ThemeScope lists every surface and text value for both modes, plus the brightness ranges, middle-grey easing and contrast targets, which theme.rs encodes nearly verbatim.

well_defined.name: Edge releases and self-update
well_defined.why: Version numbering, asset names, checking cadence, staging and swap-on-quit are precisely defined and followed by version.rs and self_update.rs.

well_defined.name: Prompt mode (chat input, sending, queue, message list)
well_defined.why: Every control, label, shortcut, lane rule, colour transition and state change is spelled out, down to tooltips and how persistence behaves across restarts.

well_defined.name: Divergence analysis
well_defined.why: It defines the agent prompt contract, how every measure is calculated, the score thresholds, report layout, tree behaviour and each tooltip's text.

well_defined.name: Container environment
well_defined.why: It lists exactly what is mounted, read-only or read-write, per kind of run, plus path mapping, volumes, Podman failure handling and image rebuild triggers.

well_defined.name: Theme
well_defined.why: It gives hex values for every role in both modes, contrast minimums, brightness ranges with exact step limits, and bevel and elevation strengths.

well_defined.name: Editor
well_defined.why: Key handling, the 80-column ruler, conflict and merge dialogs, rename following and the LSP message flow are all given exactly.

well_defined.name: Ribbon
well_defined.why: Button sizes, the 74 px maximum height, divider dimensions, collapse behaviour and per-tab command lists are fixed numerically.

less_defined.name: Rendering and layout infrastructure
less_defined.why: Virtualized row measuring, hit-area arbitration, the inline-code markdown workaround and the per-frame budgets are only described as outcomes (smooth, steady, never jumping), so measured_list.rs, hit_areas.rs and markdown.rs fill in the mechanisms themselves.

less_defined.name: Parsing harness and shell output
less_defined.why: The spec says which files count as referenced or written and that every harness's events read into one reply, but not how Codex and OpenCode JSON or arbitrary shell commands are parsed, which shell_paths.rs and harness.rs work out on their own.

less_defined.name: File watching and refresh mechanics
less_defined.why: The spec only asks that things follow the disk 'within a couple of seconds'; the shared notify watcher, rename heuristics and 2-second polling in disk_watch.rs, diff_view.rs and git_panel.rs are implementation choices.

less_defined.name: Harness catalog sources
less_defined.why: The catalog scope names where skills and agents come from but not how they are discovered on disk or which built-in agents exist, so harness_mentions.rs scans directories itself and hard-codes a built-in list.

less_defined.name: Test tooling
less_defined.why: Beyond the general rules in the EdgeReleasesScope (fake what you need, no fixed waits), helpers like double_borders.rs, frame_image.rs and test_scripts.rs have no spec behind them.

less_defined.name: Agent skills and lib anchors
less_defined.why: BuildScope, BuildApplication and the abstract Concept, Scope, Shape and Component anchors are short and general, and nothing in the application traces to them.

less_defined.name: LSP concept and chat input basics
less_defined.why: Parts such as the LSP pitch, 'auto-focused' and 'syntax highlighting via the tree-sitter grammar' are one-liners that leave the details to the implementation.

less_defined.name: Message list sub-shapes
less_defined.why: SentPrompt, OutputTable, Links and ReferencedSpec are single sentences that rely on other scopes for every detail.

less_defined.name: Project locations listing
less_defined.why: It doesn't say how hidden files, symlinks or nested .gitignore files interact, and the code has several separate file walkers that each fill this in.

less_defined.name: Theme surface roles
less_defined.why: The file tree, tables and ribbon use a darkest surface (#111111) and ribbon greys that the theme's ladder never defines.
